rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Walked every pronoun/demonstrative/definite-noun across all 9 chunks in reading order. Closest calls, all stay inside: (a) chunk 0 L7 'Come to Module 1 with the repo picked, the curated skills installed, and one trivial bug' -- definite articles with no prior antecedent at the very first chunk, but this is the chunk-0 lede/title preview construction the rule names as non-violating; each item is elaborated by its own later chunk (repo: chunk 2, skills: chunk 5, bug: chunks 1/6). (b) chunk 1 L22 'Plus the repo itself (picked next)...' and 'The curated security skills install when you extract the bundle' -- 'the repo' and 'the bundle' are forward-pointing, but 'the repo' ties to chunk-0's lede noun reused (carve-out) and reading-order-marked ('picked next'); 'the bundle' resolves two chunks later at chunk 5's own header and doesn't gate this sentence's point (skills auto-install at extraction). (c) chunk 6 L62 'if it dumps all four criteria at once' names 'four criteria' two lines before the same-chunk fenced prompt (L64) that enumerates them -- same-chunk resolution, parallels rule 12's same-chunk carve-out. Sequential resolutions confirmed elsewhere: chunk 3 L40 'the repo you just picked' -> chunk 2; chunk 6 L66 'the candidate-bug screen' -> L60/62 in-chunk; chunk 8 L80 'The bug you picked' -> chunk 6.

Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md --links` this session -> both off-file links named not located: chunk 2 L34 '[build one from zero](.../build-a-project-from-zero.md)' names the destination in the link text; chunk 7 L76 'Simon Willison, [Vibe engineering](...)' names author and title in the same sentence. Grepped body for cross-file positional phrasing ('the opening lecture said', 'earlier in this training') -- zero hits. Prework is M0, first file in the training's include order, so no prior-file callback is even possible.

All 9 chunks carry a self-carrying claim or instruction of their own (task-size inventory, repo-pick criteria, an open-session step, a download step, an extract-and-install step, a screen-and-confirm step, a pre-read pointer, a bring-to-M1 list). None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Checked all 8 body headers against their own chunk content. Closest-to-violating: chunk 4 '3. Get the content folder onto your laptop' (L43) -- its content (L45, L49) only asks the student to fetch the `.tar.gz` archive; it becomes an actual folder on disk only after chunk 5's extraction step. Stays inside: nothing in the chunk contradicts the header, chunk 5's own header ('4. Extract the bundle...') makes the two-step split explicit to the reader, and 'folder' names the well-understood eventual outcome rather than a false claim about this slide alone. Every other header (chunk 1 'Bring real work' -> 4-tier task inventory; chunk 2 '1. Pick THE repo' -> repo-pick criteria; chunk 3 '2. Open a Claude Code session...' -> open-session instruction; chunk 5 '4. Extract the bundle and install the curated skills' -> extract+install; chunk 6 '5. Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness' -> L60 restates both halves directly; chunk 7 'Pre-read before Module 1' -> Willison read; chunk 8 'Bring to Module 1' -> the bug + the opening question) matches its content exactly.

Per sub-item, checked across all 9 chunks: 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction -- `grep -inE 'Not [A-Za-z].*\. Not [A-Za-z]'` over body -> 0 hits. Anaphora/epistrophe triples -- none found (no repeated sentence-start or sentence-end pattern across 3+ clauses). Self-grading superlatives -- `grep -inE 'one of the (most|best)|most useful|most important'` -> 0 hits; closest non-hit is L70 'Small steer, small trick' which describes, doesn't grade, the tip just given. Number + own retraction -- none found; every number (a few lines, 50 lines, three candidates, 30 to 120 minutes) is stated once and stands, no walk-back. Abstraction-noun stacks -- none found; nouns used are concrete (repo, bundle, skills, tarball, bug, tests). Verb triplets with an empty leg -- none found (no triplet construction present at all).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `sed -n '1,83p' prework.md | grep -inE '\b(surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|beat|mood|connections)\b'` -> 2 hits, both 'surface': L17 'external or user-facing surface' and L29 'enough surface area for rules and memory to land on'. Both stay inside -- these are the ordinary SWE idioms 'user-facing surface' / 'surface area' (cf. 'attack surface', 'API surface'), distinct from the rule's own targeted metaphor ('writing surface', the curriculum-authoring term); AE101's engineer-IC register carve-out applies directly. No hit on compendium/firing/forcing function/beat/mood/Connections-as-proper-noun anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -nE '\*\*' prework.md` over the raw body: chunk 1 L15-18 carry one short (<=4-word) bold handle per bullet ('Trivial bug', 'A small multi-file task', 'A small feature', 'A bigger piece') labelling four task-size entries a reader scans to find their own size -- the reading-list/menu waiver applies by function (a task-size inventory meant to be scanned for an entry point, not read as one narrative sentence), each bold is well under the <=5-word handle cap, and no whole-sentence bold appears. Prework's own maintainer block (L92) already rules the §34 floor-ceiling exception N/A on this section, so the bold present is judged solely on the menu-waiver, not on §34, and it clears on function. Chunk 3 L38 '**Session**' and chunks 4-6 (raw L47/55/64/68 are bare `{{prompt:}}` markers, not literal bold in source) carry no non-widget bold to budget. Chunk 7 L76 carries exactly one bolded element, '**Read:**' (1 word, title left plain) -- the literal sanctioned reading-list shape. No chunk exceeds budget.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 8 body headings are imperative/phase-label style ('Bring real work', '1. Pick THE repo' ... '5. Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness', 'Pre-read before Module 1', 'Bring to Module 1') matching the exercise-heading convention -- prework is a task walkthrough, not a lecture, so the declarative-claim requirement doesn't bind. No slide here is a law/consolidation moment where the header IS the teaching; 'Pre-read before Module 1' and 'Bring to Module 1' are the rule's own orientation/catalogue-label carve-out shape, not mislabelled claims.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all three classes against every bullet/sentence in all 9 chunks. (a) doctrine restatement -- none; prework is pure M0 logistics with no prior lens/split/law to re-announce, and the 4 task-size bullets (chunk 1) and 3 repo-criteria bullets (chunk 2) each add a distinct move/object. (b) self-referential design commentary -- none; no sentence tells the student they are inside a pedagogy or names the curriculum's own design intent. (c) aphorism kicker -- closest candidate chunk 6 L70 'Small steer, small trick. A minute here, another there.' -- stays inside: it is concrete to the specific AskUserQuestion tip just given (L66-68), not a restatement of the header or a `**The point:**`-style line. `grep -rn 'small steer\|small trick' curriculum/` confirms this phrasing is not a coined term restated elsewhere in the corpus (self-hits only). No bullet meeting the 'carries nothing' bar found.
